video_title: Decoding the Kawhi Leonard Investigation, with DeMaurice Smith | PTFO

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the reality of 'independent' investigations in sports
quotes.excerpt: stop thinking that it's independent. Start asking questions, is it independent of whom?

text_blocks.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
text_blocks.text: The first thing that every fan should do when they hear the word independent is stop thinking that it's independent. Start asking questions, is it independent of whom?

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Adam Silver clarifies his role in the Clippers investigation
quotes.excerpt: I am not conducting the investigation, nor is the league office, that's being conducted by the Wachtell law firm
quotes.quote: I am not conducting the investigation, nor is the league office, that's being conducted by the Wachtell law firm independent of the league. Of course, as I've said previously, we all have an interest in wrapping this up, and I think I most recently said in an interview that I'm hopeful that it will wrap up this summer. So that would continue to be the goal here, and I just want to clarify, so everyone understands, the league did not pause the trade. The parties to the trade made a decision not to go forward given that the investigation remained open.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the fundamental role of a Department of Justice lawyer
quotes.excerpt: the role of a Department of Justice lawyer is to simply ensure that the dictates of the Constitution are followed
quotes.quote: The role of a Department of Justice lawyer is to simply ensure that the dictates of the Constitution are followed. And it's a rare day that you have a job like that.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on his role representing corporations and individuals in white-collar crime
quotes.excerpt: I co-chaired the white-collar crime, representing businesses, individuals who allegedly created offenses
quotes.quote: I co-chaired the white-collar crime, representing businesses, individuals who allegedly created offenses. It was primarily a business practice, but for the almost 10 years that I was a partner, you're representing large corporations, pharmaceutical companies, defense contractors, either in the middle of a criminal investigation or they think that they have uncovered some sort of criminal problem. And you're hired to do one of two things. Either A, if it comes to the attention of the government, obviously you are the defense lawyer for the company. If the company thinks that they are aware of criminal activity that violates the securities laws, they might ask you as a partner to do an internal investigation that we would call an independent investigation that would be designed to uncover who, when, where, what.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the reality of being paid by the company during internal investigations
quotes.excerpt: let's level set, you're being paid by the company.
quotes.quote: Let's level set, you're being paid by the company.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the lack of transparency in internal investigations
quotes.excerpt: the results of that internal independent investigation has never been released.
quotes.quote: There was a long-term investigation actually done by a former partner of mine, Beth Wilkinson. We were both partners together at Latham and Watkins. She had started I think the investigation when she was representing or hired by the Commanders. Later on, she was hired by the league. But if you remember, the results of that internal independent investigation has never been released.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith advises fans to question the independence of investigations
quotes.excerpt: start thinking that it's independent. Start asking questions, is it independent of whom?
quotes.quote: So the first thing that every fan should do when they hear the word independent is stop thinking that it's independent. Start asking questions, is it independent of whom? Is it independent of the general counsel? Probably not. Is it going to be released to the public? We don't know. So instead of just adopting this word independent as if it were some sort of magical, singular, truth-facing investigation that will then be released to the public so that everybody can see exactly what happened, that is probably not necessarily the case.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the limitations of independent investigators
quotes.excerpt: independent investigators for a corporation cannot compel people to talk to them.
quotes.quote: Independent investigators for a corporation cannot compel people to talk to them. And you've cleverly pointed it out, there could be people in the course of this investigation who will not talk to Wachtell Lipton. If you're an employee, you have to comply with the internal investigation or risk getting fired if you work for the NBA in some capacity.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the consequences of not cooperating with internal investigations
quotes.excerpt: if an employee does not want to talk to you, the outcome there is someone makes a decision
quotes.quote: If an employee does not want to talk to you, the outcome there is someone makes a decision whether or not that employee is going to be fired.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the privilege of internal investigation reports
quotes.excerpt: the first draft of that internal investigation is privileged. 100% privileged.
quotes.quote: The reason why the general counsel is coordinating this investigation is I promise you, the first draft of that internal investigation is privileged. 100% privileged. Two things fall into the broad realm of privilege if you're a lawyer. One, I'm representing you, our conversation is confidential, it's privileged. Second, large category is if I'm doing work to help you as my client, the work that I generate we call attorney work product, which is also privileged. Where this investigation would probably fall into. Later on, the general counsel or the company or the CEO or the board of directors can make a decision that they want to make portions or all of this internal investigation non-privileged. But in all likelihood, it's going to be privileged up until that point.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the scope of attorney-client privilege
quotes.excerpt: I'm representing you, our conversation is confidential, it's privileged.
quotes.quote: I'm representing you, our conversation is confidential, it's privileged. Second, large category is if I'm doing work to help you as my client, the work that I generate we call attorney work product, which is also privileged.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the union's duty to represent players
quotes.excerpt: the player has a duty of fair representation that he can be defended by his union
quotes.quote: The player has a duty of fair representation that he can be defended by his union and has to be defended by its union. But the salary cap violation makes it far more complicated because the union is a party to the agreement that creates the salary cap.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the antitrust exemption for sports leagues
quotes.excerpt: the leagues have an antitrust exemption. And that means for everybody out there, the leagues can operate
quotes.quote: The leagues have an antitrust exemption. And that means for everybody out there, the leagues can operate in ways that normal businesses can't. They literally have a defined market. They have cornered the market on whatever it is, basketball, football, hockey, baseball. What the law says is that if you have an antitrust exemption, then you must also have a union. And that union is allowed to come together with its members and with you create a collective bargaining agreement.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the consequences of failing to enforce the salary cap
quotes.excerpt: the day that they know that they have leverage over you to not hold them accountable
quotes.quote: The day that they know that they have leverage over you to not hold them accountable is the day the union has lost everything.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the danger of owners controlling the market
quotes.excerpt: if you didn't have a cap and the owners controlled and cornered the market, they could set a price
quotes.quote: If you didn't have a cap and the owners controlled and cornered the market, they could set a price that is far below what they're paying because of the cap. The union prevents that because it means that when they are negotiating salaries and things like healthcare and protection and pensions and things like that, you get to represent the entire body.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the importance of enforcing collective bargaining agreements
quotes.excerpt: every time you get done with a CBA at the end of those negotiations, the first thing
quotes.quote: Every time you get done with a CBA at the end of those negotiations, the first thing that the league ensures is that there is going to be a union. Why? Because if there is no union, they worry about losing their antitrust protection.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the importance of rule-following in sports
quotes.excerpt: the fundamental necessary ingredients for sport is fairness and rule following.
quotes.quote: The fundamental necessary ingredients for sport is fairness and rule following. Entertainment does not. Entertainment only asks for an audience.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the dual nature of salary caps
quotes.quote: It's both. It's absolutely both. And again, it's just like the draft. And every now and then, you would hear players, well, you know, D, I don't like to have the draft. The draft should be the free market. Again, just replay the same hypothetical that we went with. You would play for $100,000, $200,000 because you can't get any more money anywhere else. And if that's the case, the bad guys win.

quotes.speaker: DeMaurice Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMaurice Smith on the danger of owners violating salary cap rules
quotes.excerpt: if you are unwilling to enforce the rules of the salary cap, now team A, B, C, D
quotes.quote: If you are unwilling to enforce the rules of the salary cap, now team A, B, C, D and E make deals to circumvent the salary cap. And now you're in a position where you are perpetuating inequity in the system for which you are a co-owner.
